summary: Bulk ER: merge-function (representative vs union) x algorithm (R-Swoosh transitive closure vs G-Swoosh).
note: G-union 10k exceeded 90min timeout; the 4k row is the same-scale control for G-vs-R with union. All runs: same synthetic data seed=42, dup-rate=0.04, tau=0.85, 384-d hashing embedder, overlap=2.
key_findings: Union merge is essentially FREE in the R-Swoosh (transitive-closure) path: R-union 10k = 148.4s vs R-rep 10k = 154.8s (recall 1.0 either way).

Union merge is ~62x SLOWER in the G-Swoosh path at 4k: swoosh stage 399.6s (union) vs 6.4s (rep). 126k re-scores vs 14.6k, because synthetic union representatives are new dict objects that never hit the one-shot pre-score cache.
Union + G-Swoosh recovers recall to 1.0 (vs G-rep 0.956 at 4k / 0.882 at 10k): the Union-Class existence lift makes G-Swoosh's re-matching meaningful again.
R-Swoosh (either merge) remains the pragmatic default: ~150s for 10k with recall 1.0; G-Swoosh rep is 171.8s with recall 0.882; G-Swoosh union is impractical at 10k (timed out > 90min).
